title: Through every point of the image of a flat finitely presented map there is a locally quasi-finite flat chart

standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma that the Cohen-Macaulay locus of a flat finitely presented morphism is open and meets every fibre in closed points meeting the image condition (same chapter, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-open) and the CM slice lemma producing a locally quasi-finite chart through a CM point (lemma-slice-CM, same chapter); cited inputs with the assembly written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Note X_s is nonempty since s lies in the image of f.
Pick a closed point x of X_s at which f is Cohen-Macaulay using the open-CM-locus lemma.
Apply the CM slice lemma at x and set S' = Z to obtain the required chart.

proof_roadmap.step: Choose a closed CM point of the fibre.
Cut out the locally quasi-finite slice through it and take it as S'.

difficulty_reason: Given a flat, locally finitely presented morphism f : X -> S and a point s in the image, the lemma produces a commutative triangle with g : S' -> S flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, with s in the image of g and a map S' -> X over S, i.e. an fppf chart of s that is moreover locally quasi-finite and lands inside X. The retained proof is written out in three moves: the fibre X_s is nonempty, the open-ness-of-CM-locus lemma for flat finite presentation supplies a closed point x of X_s where f is Cohen-Macaulay, and the CM slice lemma then yields Z -> S etale-in-the-slice sense through x; setting S' = Z concludes. Retained author proof at lines 6451-6458.
